newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican tax collectors go on strike over bombings.
newsitem.headline: Corsican tax collectors go on strike over bombings.

text.p: Tax-collectors on the French Mediterranean island of Corsica went on strike on Monday in protest at a wave of separatist bombings against public buildings, including tax offices.
Tax offices across the island were forced to close after the CGT and Force Ouvriere unions called the 24-hour protest.
The strikers demanded tighter security and urged the state to hunt for the authors of the bombings and bring them to justice.
The bombings have occurred chiefly at night when offices were closed down and have rarely caused casualties.
A bomb blast during the night blew out windows and wrecked computers at the offices of the regional edition of the Marseille-based newspaper Le Provencal, in the northern Corsican city of Bastia.
Police said three people were slightly injured by flying glass.
No one immediately claimed responsibilty for the attack but it bore the hallmarks of separatists who are waging a bombing campaign to demand more autonomy from France for Corsica.
